Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and two asks came up that we need to resolve before procurement can finish the PO: 

1) Retention: we use historical inference telemetry for MLP analytics and would like a 5-year retention carve-out for aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry used in our internal analytics (vs. the 13‑month default in the DPA).

2) Subprocessors: we rely on a metrics vendor (CloudMetrics Inc.) to host and visualize model telemetry. They are not currently listed in the DPA subprocessor addendum. Acme needs confirmation they can be added as a permitted subprocessor and a short description of the data they receive.

I've attached our marked-up DPA with the proposed language and a spreadsheet listing the subprocessor. Can Product/Security sign off or flag technical blockers? Procurement wants to know if this will change pricing or SLA.

Attachments: acme_dpa_redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 1 page redline), acme_subprocessor_list.xlsx (xlsx)

Regards,

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can Product confirm whether 5-year retention for aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry is technically feasible...

Short answer: yes, with constraints. Notes from infra/product: 
- We already store aggregated inference telemetry (per-customer) in a telemetry service with configurable retention windows. Default is 13 months, we support custom windows per tenant via a retention flag.
- For a 5-year retention we must ensure:
  * the stored data is aggregated/pseudonymized (no user PII or raw prompts). We can apply additional sanitization on ingest — strip prompt text, hash identifiers, and only retain derived metrics (latency, token counts, model id, top-level event tags).
  * KV cache and model context are NOT part of telemetry and are never included.
  * Storage costs scale linearly — for a tenant the delta from 13 months -> 60 months is ~3.7x storage for telemetry shards. For Acme's forecasted volume this maps to approx $600/mo incremental on top of their committed tier (estimate, pricing to be validated by sales).
- Implementation impact: small config change + data-migration plan for existing telemetry they want preserved (we can backfill but it requires a 2–3 day job and short maintenance window).

Ask: If Security/Legal confirm controls, Product can sign off on feasibility. I'll draft the exact sanitization paragraph to insert into the DPA redline.

— Dev
Senior Product Manager, Telemetry
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: analytics retention & subprocessor exception for Acme

Marcus / team — thanks for the ping and the attachments. Quick legal/compliance take: 

1) Retention redline: we can allow a tenant-specific retention override for aggregated telemetry but must include explicit language that: 
   - Data must be pseudonymized and cannot be used to reconstruct user prompts or PII;
   - Retention is limited to aggregated/derived telemetry (define list: token counts, latency, model id, event tags);
   - Customer bears incremental storage costs for extended retention unless otherwise negotiated.

2) Subprocessor (CloudMetrics): we need a short description of the exact data elements CloudMetrics will receive and an assurance they meet our baseline security posture (SOC2 Type II or equivalent). We can include a subprocessor approval condition: allowed provided CloudMetrics executes a standard data processing addendum and completes our security questionnaire.

3) Contract language: see suggested clause to add to the DPA (I'm pasting a short clause I will also add to the redline file):
   "For the avoidance of doubt, Redwood may permit a Customer to request a tenant-specific retention window for aggregated telemetry. Such requests must be documented in the applicable order and are subject to (i) Redwood's data minimization and pseudonymization requirements, (ii) an executed subprocessor DPA where applicable, and (iii) Customer acknowledgement of potential cost impact."

I'm putting a tracked change into acme_dpa_redline_v3.pdf and linking a DocuSign flow for any carve-outs that require exec sign-off.

DocuSign (proposed exception flow): https://docusign.redwood.company/exceptions/ACME-2027-059

— Neha
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick Security checklist for approving a 5-year aggregated retention + CloudMetrics as a subprocessor: 

Mandatory controls before sign-off:
- Data minimization & sanitization verified by Product (Dev) — sample pipeline config and an example sanitized record.
- Per-tenant encryption keys or logical separation (we can use our current KMS + tenant key wrap).
- Subprocessor due diligence: SOC2 report from CloudMetrics or equivalent, and an executed subprocessor addendum.
- Access controls: restrict CloudMetrics access to only the aggregated dataset (no raw prompt access), with audit logging enabled and quarterly access reviews.

If Product provides a sanitized sample and CloudMetrics provides SOC2, Security can approve operationally. Legal will need to own the contract clause and the DocuSign exception flow.

I'll mark security_hold = cleared conditionally once I see the sample + SOC2.

— Evelyn
